decision: Added linkedin_leads connector (LinkedIn Lead Sync API) for consented lead data; refused to build any arbitrary people-search / PII-harvesting capability.
context: User asked for a tool to "search people by N filters and return their mobile + email." DECLINED that framing: LinkedIn exposes no people-search-with-PII API (deliberately withheld for privacy/ToS); faking it via scraping violates LinkedIn's User Agreement + GDPR/CCPA and would get the app banned; a user being authenticated does NOT authorize extracting third parties' private contact info (the data subjects haven't consented). Redirected to the LEGITIMATE path: the Marketing Lead Sync API, which returns leads that members VOLUNTARILY submitted to the user's own Lead Gen Forms (first-party, consented; includes the email/phone they chose to share). Built linkedin_leads (separate connector, MARKETING category, scope r_marketing_leadgen_automation, needs the LinkedIn-approved Lead Sync product): 5 read-only actions (list_lead_forms, get_lead_form, list_lead_responses, get_lead_response, list_leads). Key design: lead answers are keyed by integer questionId; meaning (EMAIL/PHONE_NUMBER) lives on the form — list_leads fetches the form (cached) and joins answers→labeled fields. Doc-verified against LinkedIn's canonical Lead Sync docs (2026-06-20) + 19 respx tests (incl. proving httpx preserves Rest.li union query encoding); Tier 2 "doc" pending live verification with real leads. Catalog 74→75 connectors, 1530→1535 actions. Same vendor-family-split pattern as Google (gmail/gdrive/...): linkedin (member) + linkedin_leads (marketing) are separate connectors. Related: [[D000001]] LinkedIn member Tier-1.

decision: Hardened linkedin_leads after a 6-agent adversarial audit vs LinkedIn's live Lead Sync docs — fixed the leadType enum (no 'ORGANIC'), multiple-choice field resolution, and join robustness.
context: User asked for a confidence assessment of linkedin_leads without live verification. Ran a 6-dimension adversarial audit (9 agents) re-checking the code against LinkedIn's canonical Lead Sync docs (not the respx tests' circular assumptions). Audit CONFIRMED the core is doc-correct: field projection (reads only default-returned native fields, avoids projection-gated decorations — no silent-empty), Rest.li query encoding matches LinkedIn's published samples byte-for-byte, version 202606 is current, scope r_marketing_leadgen_automation correct+sufficient, response parsing, pagination, single-GET envelopes. Fixed 4 VERIFIED defects: (1) HIGH — LeadType enum has NO 'ORGANIC'; real enum is {SPONSORED, COMPANY, EVENT, ORGANIZATION_PRODUCT}; added client-side enum validation + owner↔leadType pairing guard (SPONSORED↔sponsoredAccount; COMPANY/EVENT/ORGANIZATION_PRODUCT↔organization) so organic-form users no longer get silent-empty results or an opaque 400. (2) MEDIUM — multiple-choice/picklist answers were dropped from the resolved `fields`; now parse form question options (id→label) and resolve them. (3) Hardening — now parse + use Answer.name (LinkedIn echoes it, default-returned) as a join fallback so field resolution survives any questionId-join surprise. (4) LOW — corrected the r_ads scope docstring (r_ads can read forms but NOT lead responses). 25 respx tests (was 19); full suite 2458 pass. ONE residual unknown only live data settles: whether answer.questionId == form question.questionId (doc says yes via 'long' foreign-key; the docs lack a single-form pairing example) — the name-fallback + question_<id> degradation make this safe either way. Connector stays Tier 2 'doc' until the Lead Sync product is approved + verified against real leads (live-verify is currently blocked: the user's Lead Sync product returned unauthorized_scope_error — not yet approved by LinkedIn). Lock D000002 was temporarily toggled (with user consent) to apply these fixes, then re-locked. Related: [[D000002]].

decision: LinkedIn connector roadmap (surveyed 2026-06-20): buildable next = linkedin_conversions (self-serve, verifiable today) + linkedin_media (image/video/doc posts); approval-gated = Community Management (linkedin_org_*) + Advertising (linkedin_ads); off-limits = DMs/people-search/profile-enrichment/connections/follower-PII.
context: 6-agent adversarial survey of LinkedIn's API families vs the live docs (li-lms-2026-06). SELF-SERVE (no LinkedIn review): (1) linkedin_conversions — user HAS the Conversions API product AND a self-serve 'Direct API for Advertisers' non-expiring token (Campaign Manager > Signals Manager > Direct API); caller supplies hashed ids, no PII read-out; THE best next connector because it's the only one buildable AND live-verifiable today. (2) linkedin_media — image/document/video upload + post (multi-step initialize→PUT→finalize), the biggest gap in the text-only linkedin connector; works with self-serve w_member_social (note: w_member_social is WRITE-ONLY on the versioned /rest gateway, can't GET /rest/images). (3) extend linkedin with OIDC userinfo/id-token validation (S). (4) linkedin_verified — Verified on LinkedIn, Dev tier self-serve, 2 GETs (S). APPROVAL-GATED (user requested products, need LinkedIn review like Lead Sync): Community Management family — linkedin_org (org lookup + list_my_admin_roles, the prerequisite), linkedin_org_posts (post AS the page), linkedin_org_engagement (comment/react as page; uses NEWER r_/w_organization_social_feed scopes, distinct from _social), linkedin_org_analytics (follower/share/page stats; rw_organization_admin); Advertising — linkedin_ads (accounts/campaigns/creatives, rw_ads, heavy Rest.li patch/batch tax) + linkedin_ads_reporting (r_ads_reporting, fits_our_model=false due to non-standard Rest.li); linkedin_audiences (DMP, partner-only Audiences program); linkedin_events; linkedin_member_portability (DMA, EEA/Swiss members, self-data only). OFF-LIMITS (partner-only/closed/prohibited, doc-confirmed — reaffirms [[D000002]]): DMs/Messaging (approved partners + human-in-loop-per-message rule), arbitrary people search (no full-DB API; SNAP-partner-only), profile enrichment from person URN (restricted scope + STORAGE BAN on non-authenticated members + per-app-opaque IDs), connection lists (r_1st_connections partner-gated), follower member-level PII, scraping. Version churn: pin Linkedin-Version (202606 current), rotate ~12mo. Only Open Permissions (self-serve) member scopes: openid/profile/email + w_member_social.

decision: LinkedIn is organized Google-style: separate connectors split by CREDENTIAL/product family, each holding all capabilities its token reaches. Final structure: linkedin (member — profile/posts/comments/reactions + MEDIA), linkedin_leads, linkedin_conversions, linkedin_org (Community Mgmt consolidated), linkedin_ads. Media folds INTO linkedin (not a separate linkedin_media).
context: User asked why not one mega-connector with all capabilities. Decision: the connector boundary is the CREDENTIAL, not the brand — same token → one connector with all those capabilities; different token/product/approval → separate connector. Two hard technical reasons a mega-connector fails: (1) ToolKit holds ONE credentials value per connector, but LinkedIn surfaces need DIFFERENT tokens (member OAuth w_member_social vs the Conversions Direct-API non-expiring token vs marketing-scoped OAuth) — most actions would 403; (2) ONE verification_status per connector breaks the verification-honesty rule when surfaces have different tiers (linkedin live, linkedin_leads doc). Same rationale Google is split into gmail/gdrive/gcalendar/etc. Refines the roadmap [[D000004]] by CONSOLIDATING: fold linkedin_media into linkedin (same member token, same /rest/posts surface — just richer posting), and collapse the 4 linkedin_org_* into one linkedin_org. First execution step: add image/document/video upload + media-post to the existing Tier-1 linkedin connector (self-serve w_member_social). Reaffirms [[D000002]] boundary (no people-search). Supersedes the over-granular 10-connector list in D000004.

decision: Chaos/resilience-hardened contactout + lusha: found 13 real defects via an adversarial chaos sweep (probe harness + 8-dimension discovery workflow) that the respx happy-path tests missed, and fixed all of them. Key fix: each _request scrubs its OWN credential from raised errors (the pattern-based redactor can't catch a custom api_key/token echoed back by a server).
context: User asked to "do the chaos testing" then "u run it and find issues". Built /tmp probe harness (deleted) that drove both connectors against transport failures, full HTTP status matrix, malformed/misshapen bodies, hostile inputs, credential-echo, pagination loops, lifecycle misuse — classifying each outcome as TYPED/RETURN (good) vs BUG/HANG/LEAK (bad). Found 13/46 BAD; after fixes 0/46. Defects + fixes: (1) HIGH credential leak — server echoing the connector's own key into an error body leaked it (the http_errors pattern redactor only knows fixed prefixes like ghp_/sk-/Bearer, not a custom key value) → added scrub_secret(self._credentials) applied by wrapping the whole _request in `except ToolsConnectorError`. (2) httpx.InvalidURL from control-char path params (job_id/filter_type f-string interpolation) escaped the except blocks (InvalidURL is NOT under TransportError) → added except httpx.InvalidURL→ValidationError + a catch-all except httpx.HTTPError→TransportError + except RuntimeError (closed client)→ConnectionError. (3) non-numeric total/creditsCharged/total_results crashed int()/`<` (TypeError/ValueError/OverflowError incl NaN/Infinity) → safe_int/coerce_optional_int. (4) malformed list fields (experience as str, emails as dict) crashed Pydantic → dict_list + validate_list/safe_validate (skip bad items, keep good). (5) non-dict filters crashed {**filters}/dict() → require_dict→ValidationError. (6) empty-page-with-has_more=True spun collect() → has_more now requires bool(items). (7) action-after-teardown raw RuntimeError → typed ConnectionError. New shared module src/toolsconnector/connectors/_helpers/sanitize.py exports safe_int, coerce_optional_int, dict_list, safe_validate, validate_list, require_dict, scrub_secret. Pinned by 38 chaos tests in tests/connectors/test_people_data_chaos.py. Full suite 2593 pass. Lessons: respx happy-path tests prove internal consistency, not robustness — chaos-probe every connector; httpx.InvalidURL/RuntimeError are NOT under TransportError; the credential redactor is pattern-based and CANNOT catch a connector's own custom key — scrub it explicitly. FOLLOW-UP flagged: PaginatedList.collect() in shared types/ has no stall guard — the connector-level bool(items) guard fixes these two connectors, but a shared collect() stall guard would protect all paginated connectors.

decision: Added a universal stall guard + max_pages ceiling to the SHARED PaginatedList.collect()/collect_sync() (src/toolsconnector/types/paginated.py), fixing the latent hang flagged in D000009 for ALL ~30 paginated connectors (not just contactout/lusha).
context: Follow-up to [[D000009]]. The shared collect() looped `while len(collected) < max_items` calling anext_page() with no guard: a page with has_more=True but empty items never grows collected → infinite loop. Fix: (1) treat an empty fetched page as terminal (break), (2) max_pages ceiling default 10_000 as a hard backstop, threaded through collect_sync. The contactout/lusha call sites were already patched (has_more requires bool(items)); this protects every other paginated connector (linkedin/github/stripe/slack/…). Verified the empty-page-break does NOT truncate any connector: full suite 2596 pass across ~30 paginated connectors. Pinned by 3 tests in tests/unit/test_types.py wrapped in asyncio.wait_for (regression fails fast vs hanging the suite). Spawned-task chip task_1cff6118 dismissed (done in-session).

decision: Add `toolsconnector.auth` module in two layers: (1) request-signing providers (BearerToken, ApiKey, BasicAuth, HMACSigner, SigV4Signer, OAuth2ClientCredentials) plugged into connectors at construction; (2) flow helpers (pkce_start/exchange, device_code_start/poll, refresh_token) that return tokens and never store them — BYOK-safe.
context: Current connectors re-implement auth per-connector (scattered). Formalizing providers unblocks Tier-3 connectors needing SigV4/HMAC. Flow helpers let developers acquire tokens without coupling to any auth system. Full OAuth callbacks + token storage remain out of scope (CLAUDE.md BYOK law). Build order: providers first (unblocks AWS/Shopify/Salesforce Tier-3), flows second. Alternatives rejected: (a) full OAuth server — violates BYOK; (b) no change — leaves AWS/HMAC auth scattered. Re-examine if a connector partner requires server-side token management.
